title: Chapter 4 Quiz
description: Test your mastery of components, materials, textures, and shaders!

questions.question: What is a component in Unity?
options: A piece of functionality attached to a GameObject
questions.explanation: Components add behavior to GameObjects; they are the building blocks of everything in Unity.

questions.question: How do you add a new component to a GameObject?
options: Type its name in the Hierarchy
Drag the object into the Project window
questions.explanation: The Add Component button opens a searchable menu of all available components.

questions.question: You can copy a component's values and paste them onto another GameObject.
questions.explanation: Right-click a component and choose Copy Component, then Paste Component Values on another object.

questions.question: Which two components work together to display a 3D model?
questions.explanation: Mesh Filter holds the shape; Mesh Renderer draws it using a material.

questions.question: What does the Mesh Filter store?
questions.explanation: Mesh Filter references the mesh asset that defines the object's shape.

questions.question: What happens if you disable the Mesh Renderer component?
options: The object becomes invisible but still exists
questions.explanation: Disabling the Renderer hides the object from rendering; physics and scripts are unaffected.

questions.question: Which collider type is best for a character?
questions.explanation: Capsule Colliders are commonly used for characters because they handle slopes and movement well.

questions.question: A Mesh Collider is always the most efficient choice.
questions.explanation: Mesh Colliders are computationally heavy; primitive colliders are preferred for performance.

questions.question: What does a Rigidbody component provide?
questions.explanation: Rigidbody enables the object to be influenced by the physics engine.

questions.question: What does setting a collider as 'Is Trigger' do?
options: It allows other objects to pass through and triggers events
It destroys the object on collision
questions.explanation: A trigger collider sends OnTriggerEnter/Exit events instead of physical collision.

questions.question: A material is a combination of a _____ and its property values.
questions.explanation: Materials pair a shader with specific property configurations.

questions.question: Which property of the Standard Shader controls the base color?
questions.explanation: Albedo defines the surface's diffuse color and texture.

questions.question: How do you assign a material to a GameObject?
options: Type the material's name in the Console
Drag the material onto the object in the Scene view
Rename the object to match the material
questions.explanation: Drag & drop the material onto the object or into the Mesh Renderer's materials list.

questions.question: What does a Normal Map texture do?
options: Simulates surface bumps and details via lighting
questions.explanation: Normal maps alter per‑pixel normals to fake surface relief.

questions.question: Tiling a texture at (2, 2) makes the texture appear half the size and repeat twice on each axis.
questions.explanation: Higher tiling values make the texture repeat more, effectively shrinking the visible pattern.

questions.question: What import setting should you apply to a normal map texture?
questions.explanation: Setting the texture type to Normal Map ensures proper compression and lighting calculations.

questions.question: What is a Shader?
options: A program that runs on the GPU to calculate pixel colors
questions.explanation: Shaders determine the visual appearance of surfaces by computing color per pixel.

questions.question: Which shader ignores lighting and always shows the full color?
questions.explanation: Unlit shaders are not affected by scene lighting; they display the albedo color directly.

questions.question: In the rendering pipeline, which stage processes individual pixels?
questions.explanation: The fragment shader runs for each pixel to determine its final color.

questions.question: Materials can only be applied to objects that have a Mesh Renderer.
questions.explanation: Materials are also used by other components like Particle Systems, UI elements (via Canvas Renderer), and Line Renderers.

questions.question: What component is required to make an object fall under gravity?
questions.explanation: Rigidbody enables gravity and physics simulation.

questions.question: How can you create a new material?
options: Right‑click in the Project window → Create → Material
questions.explanation: Creating a material is done from the Project window context menu.

questions.question: What does the Metallic slider in the Standard Shader affect?
questions.explanation: Metallic controls the metal‑like reflection behavior.

questions.question: You can assign multiple materials to a single Mesh Renderer if the mesh has multiple sub‑meshes.
questions.explanation: Each material slot corresponds to a sub‑mesh index.
